title: 1545 cocoliztli epidemic in Mexico
summary: The cocoliztli epidemic struck large parts of Mexico and Guatemala from 1545 to 1550. A cemetery at Teposcolula-Yucundaa in Oaxaca is estimated to hold about 800 individuals. Ancient DNA from ten burials there contained Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C, which the researchers call a strong candidate cause, not a confirmed one. Death estimates range from five to 15 million.

where.modern_name: Near San Juan Teposcolula, Oaxaca, Mexico (the cemetery study town; the epidemic spanned a wider area)
where.historical_name: Mixteca Alta, New Spain; the epidemic affected large parts of Mexico and Guatemala

importance.justification: One of the deadliest epidemics in the early colonial Americas; ancient DNA recently gave a candidate pathogen.

audience_note: Describes a mass-mortality epidemic among Indigenous people of colonial Mexico, with death estimates in the millions. Death tolls are uncertain, and the cause is still debated.
